artists.biography:
The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion are an American alternative rock trio, formed in 1991 and based out of New York City, New York. The band consists of Judah Bauer on guitar, backing vocals, harmonica and occasional lead vocals, Russell Simins on drums and Jon Spencer on vocals, guitar and theremin. Their musical style is largely rooted in rock and roll although it draws influences from punk, blues, garage, rockabilly, soul, noise rock, rhythm and blues and hip hop. They have released seven official studio albums, collaborative records with Dub Narcotic Sound System and R.L. Burnside as well as numerous singles, out-take albums, compilations, remix albums and, in 2010, a series of expanded reissues.
Throughout the course of their career this experimental sound and occasionally unconventional recording techniques has allowed the band to work with a number of diverse artists including Elliott Smith, Beck, Solomon Burke, Steve Albini, Martina Topley-Bird and Ad Rock of the Beastie Boys.

Orange is the fourth studio album by The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion, released through Matador Records on October 11, 1994. With a runtime of 44 minutes and 44 seconds, the album showcases the band's signature blend of punk energy, blues influences, and rock experimentation that defined their approach during the mid-1990s. The project solidified their position within the alternative rock landscape of the era, building on the momentum established by their previous releases.

The album received notable critical recognition, with The Village Voice ranking it #16 among the year's best albums, indicating its significance within the contemporary music press. This accolade reflected the band's growing influence in the alternative rock scene and their ability to synthesize disparate musical influences into a cohesive and compelling sound. Orange represents a key moment in the band's career trajectory, demonstrating their artistic development and commercial viability during a particularly fertile period for independent and alternative rock labels like Matador.
